paragraphs: Parents in Ireland will pay less for childcare from September 2027. But many childcare businesses are worried about money. Services in the Government's "core funding" scheme must make their prices almost 11 per cent lower next year.

At the same time, the money the State gives to parents will go up by almost 17 per cent. Families who use a creche for long hours could save up to €2,509 a year. For full-time care, the highest price a month will go down from €959 to €750.

Children's Minister Norma Foley said the money for more than 4,600 childcare services will go up by over €170 million, to a record of more than €650 million. But the department said the services will only get back part of the money they lose from lower prices. Also, the lowest legal pay, which many workers get, will go up by almost 6 per cent.

Groups for childcare businesses said the costs of pay, energy, food and insurance keep going up. They said owners are very worried, and some services are closing. The department said 92 per cent of services are in the scheme, and it does not think many will leave.

Parents using childcare in Ireland will pay less from September 2027, but many providers say they are worried about how they will cope. Services in the Government's "core funding" scheme must cut their fees by almost 11 per cent next year.

At the same time, State subsidies for parents will rise by nearly 17 per cent. Families using long hours in a creche could save up to €2,509 a year. For full-time care, the monthly limit on fees will fall from €959 to €750.

However, the department admitted that providers would only be partly compensated for the lower fees. Meanwhile, the minimum wage, which many staff earn, is rising by almost 6 per cent.

Provider groups warned that rising costs for wages, energy, food and insurance are causing deep anxiety, and that some services are closing. The department said 92 per cent of providers have signed up to the scheme and that it does not expect large numbers to leave.
